blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Organisational design is one of the most underestimated disciplines in modern management. Most companies overhaul their structure every few years, rarely acknowledging that a new org chart alone changes very little. Structure is only one lever among several: authority, information flows, accountability, incentives and culture must all move together, or not at all.

Adaptive structures aim to balance two opposing pressures. On one side, the need for integration — alignment, scale, shared systems. On the other, the need for local responsiveness — speed, context, empowerment. Managed well, this tension is productive; managed poorly, it produces matrices where nothing gets decided.

The best structural decisions are made with a clear hypothesis about what the company must get radically better at in the next three to five years. Structure follows that hypothesis — not the other way around. Designing for yesterday's challenges is how companies end up reorganising every eighteen months, exhausting their leaders and losing institutional memory in the process.

items.q: According to the text, what does a new org chart achieve on its own?
items.why: "a new org chart alone changes very little" — o gráfico sozinho é apenas um dos vários fatores.

items.q: Which two pressures must an adaptive structure balance?
items.why: "balance two opposing pressures… integration… local responsiveness".

items.q: According to the text, structure should follow…
options: the preferences of the leadership team
a clear hypothesis about what the company must get better at
items.why: "Structure follows that hypothesis — not the other way around."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Structure should be designed backwards from strategy.
Redrawing the org chart is the fastest way to change behaviour.
Frequent restructuring carries a hidden cost.
Empowerment and alignment pull in different directions.
items.why: Inferência: o texto inteiro é um argumento contra a ideia de que o organograma, sozinho, muda comportamento.

items.q: What does "or not at all" at the end of the first paragraph suggest?
options: Some levers matter more than others
Moving only part of the system is worse than moving nothing
Culture is the only lever that counts
items.why: Inferência: os fatores movem-se juntos — mexer só em alguns é meia-mudança, que não entrega o resultado.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James aconselhando a liderança da unidade. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right — before we look at any boxes and lines, I want the leadership to answer one question: what must this business be radically better at in three years' time? Not what is broken today. Three years.

This is the third reorganisation in four years, and every one of them started with a chart. Having watched two of them from the outside, I would say the pattern is fairly clear. Authority was redrawn, but incentives were never touched, and the information the regional teams needed still sat in London. So decisions kept drifting upwards.

If we go again without agreeing the hypothesis first, we will simply reshuffle the same constraint. My recommendation is that we hold off on the structure for a fortnight. Spend that time writing down the two or three capabilities that will decide whether we win — then design backwards from those.

And whatever we land on, we live with it for five years. Every reorganisation costs you institutional memory, and this business has spent a great deal of it already.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does James want the leadership to answer BEFORE looking at the structure?
options: What is broken in the business today
What the business must be radically better at in three years
How many layers the structure should have
items.why: "what must this business be radically better at in three years' time? Not what is broken today."

items.q: According to James, what was changed in the past reorganisations — and what was not?
options: Incentives were changed; authority was not
Authority was redrawn; incentives were never touched
Culture was changed; systems were not
Headcount was cut; authority was not
items.why: "Authority was redrawn, but incentives were never touched."

items.q: Why did decisions keep drifting upwards?
options: The regional teams lacked the information they needed
The matrix had too many layers
items.why: "the information the regional teams needed still sat in London. So decisions kept drifting upwards."

items.q: What does James mean by "we will simply reshuffle the same constraint"?
options: The new structure will hit the same limitation as the old one
The same people will be moved between roles
The reorganisation will take longer than planned
items.why: Inferência: sem tratar a causa (informação e incentivos), a nova estrutura reproduz o mesmo gargalo.

items.q: How would you best describe James's tone?
options: Constructive, but sceptical about repeating the pattern
items.why: Inferência: ele critica o padrão, mas propõe um caminho concreto — não descarta a liderança.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Structure is only one lever among several." A lever is…
options: a means of producing an effect
items.why: Lever = alavanca: aquilo em que você age para produzir um efeito.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Empowerment without clear ___ creates confusion, not agility."
items.why: Accountability = responsabilização: quem responde pelo resultado.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "The ___ between London and São Paulo broke down, so the desk priced on stale data."
items.why: Information flow = fluxo de informação, o que falhou entre os dois escritórios.

items.q: Institutional memory is best described as…
options: what the organisation retains about why things were done
the length of service of the leadership team
items.why: É o conhecimento acumulado sobre as razões das decisões — o que se perde a cada reorganização.

items.q: Org design covers…
options: the chart plus authority, information flows and incentives
items.why: É a tese central da lição: o organograma é só um dos elementos do desenho.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de reestruturação. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CFO still has to sign off on the new structure." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the new model region by region." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two regional heads pushed back on the proposal." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The team agreed the plan but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "None of that will move the needle on decision speed." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
